## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Sikkhaṁpaccācikkhaṇa* (“Renouncing the training in anger”) is the tenth *saṅghādisesa* rule of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule addresses the disciplinary offense incurred when a Buddhist nun persistently declares in anger that she will renounce the training and join another religious tradition; such conduct warrants formal suspension by the community (*saṅghādisesa*) [SuttaCentral]. A complete English translation of the rule and its commentary is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. None of the sampled secondary literature passages specifically discusses this rule, as matched citations merely refer to incidental section numbers in other works.

SuttaCentral identifies exact parallels to this rule across the surviving Vinaya traditions, including the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (*pli-tv-bi-pm-ss10*) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra*, the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Ss 16* and *pm-ss16*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Ss 17* and *pm-ss17*), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Ss 14* and *pm-ss14*), Mūlasarvāstivāda in both Chinese (*Lzh Mu Bi Vb Ss 13*) and Tibetan (*xct-mu-bi-vb-ss13*), Mahāsāṅghika (*Lzh Mg Bi Vb Ss 19*), and the Sanskrit Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravādin *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* (*san-lo-bi-vb-ss19*) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse computation in DharmaNexus corroborates these cross-tradition alignments, identifying matches with the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* (similarity score up to 75) and the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records extensive text sharing with the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā*, and neighboring *saṅghādisesa* procedural formulas in both the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (rules 11–13) and the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (rules 10–13) [DharmaNexus].
